run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T09:14:14Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: frontend-proxy's RequestErrorRate alert is explained by a real error burst, not by proxy trouble: at 09:33 frontend-proxy recorded 0.724 error spans/s of 10.768 spans/s, and its access logs show GET /api/data answered 500 via_upstream by the frontend. The same 09:33 query shows the deepest failing service is ad (oteldemo.AdService/GetAds STATUS_CODE_ERROR, 0.356/s); ad's GetAds error rate was 0 through 09:22, then rose to a peak of 0.846/s at 09:30 and was 0.177/s at 09:34, while ad's GetAds p95 latency rose from 88 ms (09:15 baseline) to 583 ms (09:25). Exactly over that interval, a chaos-mesh Schedule named otel-demo-ad-jvm-return spawned a JVMChaos experiment every minute from 09:19:53 to 09:28:53, each applied to "otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg/ad" and recovered about 55 s later, and the ad container logged repeated gRPC handler exceptions. The ad pod itself was Running and ready with 0 restarts, so this is an injected JVM-level fault, not a crash. ad's flagd dependency does not explain it (ResolveBoolean error increase 0, EventStream error rate unchanged from the pre-incident baseline), and the flagd adFailure flag is off in flagd-config. The exact alert expression and the JVMChaos action/method fields could not be read, and the alert's stated start (09:14:14) precedes the observed deviation (first chaos applied 09:20:03) while a ~0.01 error spans/s baseline existed earlier; conclusion is therefore partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy recorded STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on both of its operations. The summed 5-minute error rate stayed between 0.007 and 0.017 spans/s from 08:57:14 through 09:19:14, rose to 0.178/s at 09:21:14, peaked at 1.004/s at 09:29:14 and was 0.443/s at 09:33:14; the series for span_name=ingress and span_name=router frontend egress moved identically.

At 09:33 the by-service error query returned frontend 1.392 error spans/s, frontend-proxy 0.724/s, ad 0.356/s and fraud-detection 0.004/s, while frontend-proxy's total span rate was 10.768/s; the same query returned no error series for cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, product-catalog, quote or shipping (that absence is only what this query matched, not proof of zero).

At 09:33 the error series by operation were: frontend-proxy ingress 0.368/s and router frontend egress 0.356/s; frontend GET 0.348/s, GET /api/data 0.348/s, executing api route (pages) /api/data 0.348/s and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 0.348/s; ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 0.356/s. The co-occurring frontend-side client operation named grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and ad-side server operation oteldemo.AdService/GetAds fail at the same rate.

frontend-proxy's access log for 09:29:03-09:29:08 shows GET /api/data?contextKeys=... requests answered 500 via_upstream (e.g. "GET /api/data?contextKeys=assembly HTTP/1.1" 500 via_upstream) while other endpoints such as /api/cart and /api/products/* returned 200, plus one 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}; the 500s come from the frontend upstream, not from a proxy-local failure.

ad's own GetAds error rate was 0 at 09:22:00, then 0.26/s at 09:23:00, 0.42/s at 09:24:00, 0.55/s at 09:25:00 and peaked at 0.846/s at 09:30:00, easing to 0.177/s at 09:34:00, while GetAds STATUS_CODE_UNSET fell from 0.948/s at 09:18:00 to about 0.09-0.10/s, so GetAds total throughput stayed near 0.9 spans/s and only the success/failure mix changed.

At 09:25 ad's 5-minute increase was 165.66 error spans on oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (SERVER), while ad's own client calls to flagd were not newly failing: flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase was 0 and flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream was 1.11. At 09:15, before the deviation, no oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error series existed and the same flagd series read EventStream 1.11 and ResolveBoolean 0.

A chaos-mesh Schedule named otel-demo-ad-jvm-return (namespace chaos-mesh) recorded Spawned events "Create new object: otel-demo-ad-jvm-return-<suffix>" every minute from 09:19:53 to 09:28:53 (gbjlm, 9f6n6, j2fmx, plmnp, ljkwf, dlm4f, 4x48z, m8wnc, gzz89, 2xnmj), plus lastScheduleTime updates.

Each spawned JVMChaos object started, then reported "Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg/ad" (first at 09:20:03, repeating at 09:20:57, 09:21:57 ... 09:28:55), then "Time up according to the duration" and "Successfully recover chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg/ad" about 55 s after application; the target is the ad pod's ad container.

Cluster events in chaos-mesh grouped by involvedObject kind and reason counted JVMChaos Applied 9, Started 10, TimeUp 9, Recovered 9 and FinalizerInited 18, and Schedule Spawned 10 / Updated 10 over 09:19:53-09:28:53; the only JVMChaos target names seen are otel-demo-ad-jvm-return-* .

The ad pod ad-554b849958-sk6fg was Running and ready during the incident: container ready=true, state running since 08:44:01, lastState empty, restartCount 0, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:c9d4f94314937eb3b61cf8b1672b7e87fab95442bd1d01f8d32f43a882255944.

The ad container's log contains repeated lines "Exception while executing runnable io.grpc.internal.ServerImpl$JumpToApplicationThreadServerStreamListener$1HalfClosed@..." with 95 such matching lines in the 09:23:00-09:25:00 window (5 newest at 09:24:58-09:24:59).

All 21 otel-demo pods were Running with restartCount 0 at query time, started between 08:43:58 and 08:45:52, so no pod-level crash loop or rollout occurred during the incident window; the ad pod's start time is 08:43:58.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in otel-demo contains flags adFailure (defaultVariant off, state ENABLED), adHighCpu (off), adManualGc (off), cartFailure (off), paymentFailure (off) and others; adFailure is not set on.
ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds p95 duration rose from 88.1 ms at 09:15 (pre-deviation baseline) to 583.5 ms at 09:25 and was 342.5 ms at 09:33, so the failing operation also became much slower.
frontend-proxy has exactly two span operations, ingress (server) and router frontend egress (client), so its error spans describe proxied request handling rather than an internal service of its own.

ad's dependency on flagd was not newly failing during the deviation: at 09:25 its flagd ResolveBoolean error increase was 0 while GetAds had 165.66 errors/5m, and the flagd EventStream client error series kept the same small magnitude (0.0037/s) at 09:15 before the deviation and at 09:25 during it.

fraud-detection's only error series (flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream) fluctuated at 0-0.0037/s both before 09:20 (09:09 0.0037, 09:14 0) and after (09:29 0.0037, 09:34 0), i.e. a pre-existing background series, not a deviation tied to this alert.

The ad service was not down, crashed or evicted: the pod was Running/ready with restartCount 0 and an empty lastState, all 21 otel-demo pods were Running with 0 restarts, and no Pod events for otel-demo appeared in the cluster event listing, so OOMKilled/Evicted/BackOff explanations are not supported.

The 'adFailure' feature flag (or adHighCpu/adManualGc) in flagd being enabled as the cause is not supported: the flagd-config ConfigMap read during the investigation shows adFailure defaultVariant off, and the fault was repeatedly applied directly to the ad container by JVMChaos experiments rather than by a flag value, while ad's flagd evaluation calls were not erroring.

A JVM-level fault injected into the ad service by the chaos-mesh JVMChaos children of Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-return (the name suggests a 'return'-style injection) is what makes oteldemo.AdService/GetAds fail and become slow; this fits the ±1-minute alignment of the applied/recovered chaos events with the GetAds error and p95 latency rise, but the exact injected action, class, method and return value cannot be read from the available evidence.

The frontend /api/data 500s that frontend-proxy logs and its ingress/egress error spans reflect are plausibly the downstream consequence of the ad GetAds failures, because the frontend client operation named grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and the ad server operation oteldemo.AdService/GetAds carry the same error rate as GET /api/data; span parent references were not available, so the call edge itself is inferred, not directly observed.

Stop the fault injection by disabling or deleting the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-return (and its generated JVMChaos children) in namespace chaos-mesh, then re-check that ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error rate returns to its pre-09:20 level and that frontend-proxy's ingress error rate falls; no remediation is executed in this investigation.

gaps: The Prometheus rules API returned no data for the RequestErrorRate rule (list_prometheus_rules returned an empty result with status no_data at 526d3bc8-dc0e-4aeb-86c9-1e11321d2b2f-t0:afea55e0-e1a5-47bc-b646-f6513ee76ab0 and 579a66df-dddf-4c01-8b7d-f9bb63596a37-t0:5792634c-f9ca-46af-8817-a9f1d7e4b74b), so the alert's exact PromQL, threshold semantics and 'for' duration are unknown; the alert start 09:14:14 precedes the observed error deviation (first JVMChaos applied 09:20:03) and a ~0.007-0.017 error spans/s frontend-proxy baseline existed earlier, so whether the alert was already firing on baseline noise before the chaos cannot be confirmed.

chaos-mesh custom resources (Schedule and JVMChaos) could not be read with the available Kubernetes resource kinds: the CRD jq query returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE (9cb6ab80-190c-4486-8175-3124542b403e-t0) and was not completed; the injected action, target class/method/return value, and the schedule's creation/deletion times are unknown (only its events were readable).

Jaeger trace searches for ad (2705e8f3-e23c-4577-b119-2bc670da0162-t1:96679420-a230-4afd-be14-9d722e4c2fa7, 11c7603d-4cd3-487a-ae20-ca6a062ff471-t0:be741619-039b-435a-849b-0d0bda3bbdf1), frontend (f19272aa-d3d0-4efa-844f-8da10299803a-t1:a7c6b1b9-f056-4f1c-87e0-a0aaaa71a7c2) and frontend-proxy (5926f156-175d-44ce-ac60-1971cd9f8103-t0:015c3f4b-e8b7-449c-b7d8-d59d2c7cadfc, 579a66df-dddf-4c01-8b7d-f9bb63596a37-t1:047be81e-283b-46ab-b761-9065f0c9096f) returned no traces (status no_data), so span-level status messages and parent-child references could not be inspected; the frontend-to-ad call edge is inferred from operation names and coincided error rates, not from parent references.
Metric samples end at 09:34 and JVMChaos events end at 09:28:53, so the state after 09:34 (whether the chaos schedule stopped and whether frontend-proxy's error rate recovered) is unknown.

The flagd pod's logs returned zero lines for all its containers (ec2ff7e5-30e0-464a-89c6-f888f7069e0c-t0:fe501234-0e18-4aeb-aec3-febb227b75ad, status no_data), so a runtime flag change through flagd could not be checked directly; the flagd-config ConfigMap is the only flag-state evidence and reflects the state at query time, not during the incident.

http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned no series in the window (ed83dbd8-ac57-4204-afc8-45476572c398-t0:e599248e-820c-497f-aa4b-4e8d2f7058ae and -t1:36b4f0de-ff94-4b62-8931-3e2e4bfdc368, both no_data), so the exact metric behind the alert annotation value 2.1111111111111107 could not be identified.

Several log queries returned no matching lines and are only stated limits, not absence proof: ad container error/exception filter over 09:08-09:16 (d5e6ca35-3f89-4f0d-806c-2e89d23f6b78-t0:ea95b136-1313-4362-9265-5eb473bd27ce, 28431220-53aa-4a3b-a39e-8671f62107df-t0:4b229a08-570b-4639-bd4e-8367f0c5af20) and the frontend container log query (e2c1d6db-9add-463a-833f-f1d1d3ac1a0a-t0:7f6f9c91-1892-44ea-977c-4ec2508df7f0); the ad and frontend-proxy log reads were also capped by their line limits (f19272aa-d3d0-4efa-844f-8da10299803a-t0:1a31efff-8dff-471f-8dbf-2aa16d74c127, d229484b-36ee-4a0c-a2ce-c921b77c0a66-t0:4369b7d9-cebc-4637-982d-99f2bc766ae7, e2c1d6db-9add-463a-833f-f1d1d3ac1a0a-t1:2e7aec7c-a9a0-41a4-b806-2163c2ed8d91, 28431220-53aa-4a3b-a39e-8671f62107df-t1:d428ba84-12bd-498a-8f84-394df7da6cd6), so earlier ad error text was not retrieved.
The change_history integration is not integrated, so no change records (person/commit/rollout) around 09:19-09:20 are available.
next_steps: Read the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-return and one of its JVMChaos children with chaos-mesh CR access to confirm the injected action, class, method and duration.
Confirm with the platform/chaos owner whether the otel-demo-ad-jvm-return schedule was intentionally started at ~09:19:53 and whether/when it was stopped or deleted.
Check the alert rule definition in the Prometheus/Alertmanager configuration to confirm the RequestErrorRate expression and why it started at 09:14:14 versus the 09:19-09:20 error deviation.
After the chaos is stopped, verify recovery of ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error rate and p95 latency and of frontend-proxy ingress/egress error spans over a fresh window.
